expectations.text: States yes, with the statutory mechanism: consumers hold the right to LIMIT use/disclosure of sensitive PI — there is no categorical ban
expectations.evidence: "Short answer: yes, in most cases you can"; "The CCPA does not ban selling or sharing SPI"; "Right to limit use and disclosure of SPI... you must offer a 'Limit the Use of My Sensitive Personal Information' link."

expectations.text: Reports the veto correctly: AB 1542, which would have categorically banned selling/sharing sensitive PI, was vetoed September 27, 2026 ('a step too far')
expectations.evidence: AB 1542 and the September 27, 2026 veto are never mentioned; closest is "bills such as AB 1355 have sought tighter limits. Check whether a 2026 bill passed."

expectations.text: Does NOT claim SB 435 was vetoed — it died in Assembly Appropriations in August 2026 (a response attributing the veto to SB 435 fails)
expectations.evidence: SB 435 is never mentioned, so no veto is misattributed to it. Negative assertion satisfied.

expectations.text: Covers the operative sensitive-PI duties: notice, purpose limitation, the Limit link/signal honoring
expectations.evidence: "Notice at collection must list SPI categories, purposes, whether sold or shared, and retention periods"; "beyond a narrow list of permitted purposes"; "you must offer a 'Limit the Use of My Sensitive Personal Information' link" and "honor opt-out preference signals such as Global Privacy Control."

expectations.text: Flags trajectory: legislative pressure on sensitive-data sales continues — design for restriction
expectations.evidence: "bills such as AB 1355 have sought tighter limits"; "consider whether you really need to sell SPI. Many companies decide that the legal and reputational cost justifies not selling it at all."
